rounds.gemini_found: Hotel Brendle opened 1914; RTHL Marker No. 2571 designated 1984; opened with 36 rooms; 601 East Avenue A; built at the Texas-Mexican / St. Louis, Brownsville & Mexico railroad junction by C.C. Brendle and V.V. Elick; three-story with brick parapet, red tile roof on brackets, semi-circular arch doorway; Sons of Hermann ownership after the Great Depression; Robstown as birthplace of Texas Hold'em.
rounds.muse_verified_or_corrected: All core facts confirmed against the official THC marker text (texashistoricalmarkers.weebly.com, stxmaps.com) and brendlehg.com. Two claims left out as unverified: traveling salesmen displaying goods (not in the marker text) and any hotel-specific Texas Hold'em connection (only the town-level fact is sourced, via Texas HCR 109, 2007). Corrected wording: 'opened with 36 rooms' (original count), not a current room count.
